survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note summarizes indicators from Education at a Glance 2025 rather than providing a student-level microdata analysis. The note reports cross-country descriptive statistics (e.g., attainment shares, unemployment rates by education level, literacy proficiency distributions from PIAAC) and does not specify any sampling-weight variables or replicate-weight procedures. Because no ILSA/PISA-style microdata model is estimated here, there is no weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT) to apply at the analysis stage. For users who would replicate the underlying indicators, the appropriate weights and replicate procedures depend on the original source study for each indicator (e.g., PIAAC for adult literacy; OECD administrative sources for labour-market outcomes), and those details are provided in the Education at a Glance 2025 Sources, Methodologies and Technical Notes.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a country note that reports indicator results (shares, gaps, trends, and literacy proficiency levels) rather than estimating a student-level model with plausible values. Missing-data handling is therefore not applicable to the note’s presentation of already-produced OECD indicators; the underlying methodological details are referenced to the Education at a Glance 2025 technical documentation.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Education at a Glance 2025 Netherlands country note synthesizes system-level and population-level education indicators using the latest available reference years. It highlights intergenerational educational inequality in tertiary attainment, unemployment and wage patterns by educational attainment, and adult literacy proficiency distributions and gaps from the OECD Survey of Adult Skills (PIAAC). It also reports trends in literacy scores across PIAAC cycles, participation in education and training by literacy level, and tertiary education progression indicators such as entry pathways, completion rates, dropout after the first year, and international student mobility. The note further summarizes education financing and teacher workforce indicators (e.g., expenditure per student, funding shares, teacher shortages/turnover, and instruction time). No student-level ML modeling, plausible-value estimation, or explicit sampling-weight application is conducted in the note; it is descriptive and points to the underlying technical documentation for indicator construction.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is sparse because this document is a descriptive OECD country note rather than an empirical large-scale assessment analysis with an explicit analytic sample, model specification, or ML pipeline. As a result, there are no student-level targets, performance metrics, or ML algorithms to populate, and the note does not report PV or missing-data handling at the analysis level. The methodological details for each indicator are deferred to the Education at a Glance 2025 Sources, Methodologies and Technical Notes and the referenced indicator tables.
